subject.title: Skipped group messages behind requireMention do not reach message hooks, which blocks full-history archive plugins

question: Should OpenClaw expose mention-skipped/pre-session inbound content to trusted installed plugins through a public read-only hook, and must that hook be gated before release?
rationale: This changes the Plugin SDK privacy boundary because plugins could observe content before current mention/session dispatch gates would expose it publicly.

options.title: Gate the public hook before landing
options.body: Add an explicit operator/plugin permission or access gate, document the payload boundary, and land the narrow hook only after that contract is visible.

options.title: Approve installed-plugin trust
options.body: Maintainers can accept that any installed plugin registering the hook may observe skipped inbound content without an extra gate.

options.title: Keep internal ingest only
options.body: Pause or reject the public hook and leave full-fidelity archive plugins dependent on internal/channel-specific integrations for now.

recommendation.title: Gate the public hook before landing
recommendation.body: Add an explicit operator/plugin permission or access gate, document the payload boundary, and land the narrow hook only after that contract is visible.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the nearest merged internal skipped-message ingest path and are the clearest history owner for deciding whether that boundary becomes public.
